228d60c372.q: What percentage of all charitable gifts in the United States come from individuals?
228d60c372.a: 64% of all charitable gifts come from people, totaling almost $400 billion. The remaining portion comes from foundations, estate gifts, and corporations. Overall, approximately 90% of giving really comes from individuals when you add up individuals' direct gifts, foundation money, and estate gifts.

3df7d8153a.q: How much did Corky Caldwell leave to Raritan Valley Community College in his estate gift?
3df7d8153a.a: Corky Caldwell, a chemist who attended community college in Iowa, left $24 million to Raritan Valley Community College in his will after taking care of his wife. The money had grown significantly from his original plan because his investments continued to appreciate over time, and the college honored him with scholarships and naming rights.

0a16395e8d.q: What percentage of affluent households give to charity compared to all income levels?
0a16395e8d.a: Among affluent households, 81% are charitable compared to about two-thirds for all income levels. Affluent households give on average about $33,000 per year, which is significantly higher than the average of 4% of income across all Americans.

77f2f8ce24.q: How much do millennials give to charity per year on average?
77f2f8ce24.a: Millennials give on average about $480 per year to charity. This is compared to Gen X giving about $732 per year, baby boomers giving about $1,200 per year, and the silent generation giving about $1,400 per year.

71dc326293.q: What share of Americans give their time to charity formally?
71dc326293.a: About 28% of adults give their time to charities formally. However, over 54% of Americans help out somebody in the community in informal ways, whether it be helping out a neighbor or tasks like pulling the mailbox to the curb for an elderly neighbor.
